title: How to calculate your Coast FIRE number in the U.S.
description: The math behind front-loading your retirement savings so you can switch to a lower-stress job sooner.
content:
Most retirement strategies focus on the finish line: saving consistently until age 65. 'Coast FIRE' (Financial Independence, Retire Early) flips this script. It asks: 'How much do I need to save *now* so that compound interest alone will hit my retirement number without me adding another penny?' Once you hit this 'Coast Number,' you don't retire immediately. Instead, you downshift. You take a lower-paying, lower-stress job that covers your daily bills, confident that your nest egg is growing in the background to cover your future. This guide teaches you how to calculate your specific freedom number.

Key Takeaways

  • The Concept: You save aggressively early in your career (20s/30s). Once you hit Critical Mass, you stop contributing to retirement entirely.
  • The Lifestyle Shift: Reaching Coast FIRE allows you to switch to part-time work, freelance, or a passion project because you only need to earn enough to cover current rent/food.
  • Compound Interest Heavy Lifting: The strategy relies on time. $100k left alone for 30 years at 7% becomes $760k. The money works harder than you do.
  • Risk Factors: It assumes market returns over a long period. If the market underperforms for 20 years, you might need to restart contributions.

Why It Matters (US Context)

In the US, Coast FIRE is particularly attractive because of the high cost of healthcare. By continuing to work a 'Barista' job or part-time corporate role, you maintain access to employer-sponsored health insurance while eliminating the pressure to save 20% of your paycheck.

The Coast FIRE Formula

The calculation works backward from your Traditional Retirement goal.

Step 1: Determine Your FI Number

How much do you need at age 65?
Rule of Thumb: Annual Spending x 25.
If you spend $60,000/year, you need $1.5 Million at age 65.

Step 2: Calculate Years to Grow

Current Age: 30.
Retirement Age: 65.
Years to Grow: 35 Years.

Step 3: Apply the Growth Rate

Assume 7% real return (inflation-adjusted). The formula is:
Coast Number = FI Number / (1 + Return)^Years

The Math: $1,500,000 / (1.07 ^ 35) = $140,500.

The Result: If you are 30 years old and have $140,500 invested, you are done saving for retirement. You can spend 100% of your paycheck for the next 35 years, and (statistically) you will still retire with $1.5M.

Execution Strategy

  1. The Sprint: Live frugally and save 50%+ of your income for 3-5 years to hit your Coast Number. This is the 'Hard Phase'.
  2. The Pivot: Once the account hits the number, change your life. Quit the stressful 60-hour/week job. Take a job paying half as much that you actually enjoy.
  3. Let it Ride: Ensure the money is invested in broad market ETFs (VTI/VOO). Do not touch it. Do not trade it.
  4. Monitor: Check annually. If the market crashes, your Coast timeline might extend. Be flexible.

Frequently Asked Questions

What about inflation?

Using a 7% 'Real' return assumption (10% nominal minus 3% inflation) accounts for this. The $1.5M target is in 'Today's Dollars'. The actual nominal number will be much higher, but purchasing power remains the target.

Does Social Security count?

Coast FIRE calculations usually ignore Social Security to be conservative. If SS exists when you retire, it is just icing on the cake.

What if I withdraw money early?

You break the compounding curve. Coast FIRE requires you to never touch the principal until traditional retirement age. Your current job must cover all current expenses.
